beats.name: hook
beats.said: Inventor bent his coaster's loop into a lumpy shape.
beats.shown: Laughing protagonist slams a mallet on a rusty rail with sparks; fast pull-back reveals a bent loop standing in a meadow.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: First upside-down ride cost him everything; rival copies it; test dummy returns crushed; he must open tomorrow.
beats.shown: Scaffold lift hill, flat-faced close-up with an empty open wallet, rival at a blueprint easel, dusk station with banner, cart with crushed green dummy.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: He hammers the loop's base gentle overnight, unsure it works; the rival slips in and squeezes it narrow.
beats.shown: Moonlit field: glowing white-hot rail and sparks, rival laughing at a telescope, loop squeezing from a circle into a narrow fairy-lit ellipse.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: Opening morning: town queues at the rival's circle; owner's cart tips toward the skinny loop; cliffhanger.
beats.shown: Bright daylight midway with confetti, crowd on the platform, rival waving in front, owner's cart rolls over the hill toward the narrow loop.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Hairpins flip fast cars; carts peak at a loop's base, where a circle's tight curve crushed the dummy.
beats.shown: Teal car and red hot rod on a hairpin road (smoke, flip), then a white-steel ring loop with a glowing speed trail.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: Flattened bottom plus the rival's squeeze lifted the hairpin to the slow top, so he floats over unharmed.
beats.shown: Camera flies through the tall loop as the red cart passes upside down with the protagonist's head hanging out, unhurt; then glides off the loop.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: The rival's cart reaches the base of his perfect circle at that exact moment.
beats.shown: Low wide meadow with a blue tower; fireball and mushroom cloud erupt; protagonist's cap rises in his cart and he turns with a smug smirk.

hook.first_frame: Laughing protagonist (round white head, red cap, blue overalls) mid-swing with a big mallet over a rusty rail in the foreground; blue sky, trees and hills behind; caption 'He' low centre.
hook.first_3s: 0-1.0 s mallet rises and slams the rail with sparks; 1.0-1.5 s fast pull-back and tilt-up reveals a lumpy bent loop in a green field (one continuous move); 1.6-2.77 s slow drift on the loop.
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title promises the payoff (the shape that saved coasters); the first line opens on the deformation itself, so the title is the answer and the line is the puzzle.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: Riders move fastest at a loop's bottom, so a circle's tight bottom curve is the dangerous spot; a tall teardrop loop moves the tight curve to the slow top.
story.protagonist: Unnamed coaster owner and inventor: red cap, overalls, flat unimpressed default face
story.authority_or_antagonist: Unnamed rival ride owner: dark pompadour, cream vest with gold trim, smug grin
story.explainer_turn: 'You see,' at 41.10 s (an earlier 'You see,' at 2.44 s is only a premise aside)

tone.humour: Dark slapstick: gleeful mallet swinging, a crushed test dummy, a fly on his nose, a nuke-sized fireball for the rival and a smug final smirk.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Deadpan narrator and an ironic reversal (the sabotage meant to kill him saves him); a self-answered rhetorical question works as a gag.
tone.dialogue_style: No character speech: one narrator voice, one rhetorical question, a 'You see' aside; characters only emote through swapped faces.

animation.body_motion: Rigged puppet on a few strong poses: mallet wind-up f6-f12, slam f18, recoil f30; heads rotate in 3D (f1865-f1877); the camera supplies most of the motion.

generation_evidence.observation: Foreground rail is defocused into orange bokeh while the character stays sharp, and sparks appear at the exact mallet contact point.
One continuous 0.35 s pull-back and tilt-up; the protagonist stays in the same spot and the rusty lattice and bent loop keep rigid, consistent perspective.
Paint-drip banner lettering keeps identical letter shapes, drips and brush texture across 5 s and a push-in; no warping or re-spelling.
Protagonist's head turns from back view (cap strap, hair) to a 3/4 face; outline, cap brim and hair stay coherent, so the head is a rigged 3D object with a toon outline.

Red UPSIDE-DOWNER cart and its lettering stay rigid and crisp through a 1.4 s swooping orbit; the same cart recurs at 13 s, 57-58 s and 62 s, and the same Ferris wheel and barn props recur across scenes.
Fireball and mushroom cloud are soft, blurred and photographic next to the crisp toon set, and sprite clouds have flat bottoms and a hard clipped edge; reads as a stock 2D VFX overlay (estimate).

Character animation frame rate (poses may be held on twos); needs frame differencing on a moving limb.
Whether the fireball is a stock video overlay or an engine particle effect.
Hidden joins inside 46.4-59.7 s and 5.0-5.5 s (very fast push-in) were not frame-checked beyond the flagged suspects; 59.4-59.9 s was checked and is continuous.
Shadows cast by characters: none visible, but characters are small in most shots.
Era is never stated: 1900s is inferred from vintage cars, costumes and loop-coaster history (estimate); chalkboard diagram and wallet photo are illegible.
